title: Four 2026 gauge replays did not resolve a daily-risk error from a fitted Gaussian serial copula
abstract: We tested serial dependence after a normal-score transform of hourly observed-minus-tide residuals at Boston, Charleston, San Diego and Eagle Point in January-September 2026. An empirical law uses all 6,552 cyclic 24-hour windows per gauge. A Gaussian copula fits their normal-score lag correlations and uses the exact same discrete hourly marginal law. Nine fixed tide shapes and three peak hourly risk levels give 108 primary conditions. Across 12 station-and-level averages, Gaussian-to-empirical daily-risk ratios range from 0.907 to 1.043. All conditional 95% intervals from 3-, 7- and 14-day blocks include zero difference. They omit fitted-model uncertainty. Mean absolute condition-level difference is 0.178 percentage point. Removing monthly means reduces the largest average deficit from 9.3% to 1.9%. A source-style correlation-weighted product rule can differ more than direct Gaussian integration in the same finite experiment. At Boston, six-hour upper-tail persistence is 66.5% against 33.1% for the fitted Gaussian pair, despite close daily risks. Tide shape can hide a joint-tail difference. This diagnostic is exploratory. The result does not identify a systematic copula error or establish its absence. It limits direct use of large theoretical dependence gaps as estimates of real ocean forecast error. These are score-space replays, not actual flood thresholds or issued forecast validation. Short records, selected gauges, overlapping windows, retrospective fits and non-stationarity limit inference. Code, exact source provenance, aggregate evidence, numerical checks and a figure are included; raw records remain external.

display.caption: Finite normal-score replay at four gauges. Left: Gaussian-copula daily risk minus empirical risk, with conditional 7-day block intervals; crosses use the source-style rule. Right: upper-tail persistence differences at 5% peak hourly risk. The intervals keep the fitted model fixed.
